NAHID NAZIA
Vs.
MOSAMMAT ABEDA CHOWDHURY AND OTHERS
full_judgment: 2. The petitioner herein as plaintiff filed Title Suit No.232 of 2004 in the Court of the Subordinate Judge, Second Court, Dhaka, for specific performance of contract. Thereafter the said suit was transferred to the Court of Joint District Judge, 5th Court, Dhaka and was renumbered as Title Suit No. 330 of 2010. The plaintiff stated, inter alia, that the land under C.S. Khatian No. 479 R.S. Dag Nos. 305 and 306 comprises total land measuring 173½ decimals out of which the suit land is 157 decimals owned and possessed by defendant No. 1 Mosammat Abeda Chowdhury and others who entered into an agreement for sale of the property with Nahid Nazia the plaintiff at a consideration of Tk. 28,91,660/- and received Tk. 15,00,000/, as earnest money and handed over possession. It was stipulated to execute and register sale deed within 15.10.1999 after receipt of the balance consideration money by defendant Nos. 1-11 and the husband of defendant Nos. 1. On 11.6.2000, 16½ decimals out of the suit land mentioned in the original agreement for sale was transferred by the husband of the defendant No. 1 from his share of the land to the plaintiff's husband by a registered .sale deed dated 08.06.2000. The period for execution of the sale deed in respect of the remaining land of the bainapatra was extended up to 15.07.2000. But the defendants failed to execute and register the sale deed within the stipulated time. Thereafter, the plaintiff repeatedly requested them to execute and register the sale deed. But the defendants on different dates took different pleas and delayed the execution and registration of the sale deed. Mr. Kamrul Hossain Chowdhury, the son of defendant No. 1 on behalf of his mother took Tk. 35,000/-from the plaintiff and assured her about execution and registration of the sale deed very soon. The plaintiff was always ready to pay the balance consideration money to the defendants. At that time the plaintiff came to know that instead of executing and registering the sale deed, defendant Nos. 1-11 were negotiating to sell the suit property for a higher price to others. Then the defendant Nos. 1-11 on 09.05.2004 served a legal notice through their Advocate intimating the plaintiff that the deed of agreement for sale is cancelled and the earnest money received is forfeited and asked her for return of the original documents which was given earlier to the plaintiff. In this way the defendants refused to execute and register the sale deed, hence the plaintiff was constrained to file the suit.
